assessed_degradation.note: Assessed degradation counts only capacity a source explicitly quantified. It is deliberately distinct from exposure, which counts capacity at disrupted sites regardless of measured loss.

recovery_stats.note: Recovery is tracked per incident and counted by DISTINCT EPISODE: a multi-day strike counts once. A median observed restoration is shown only with >= 5 independent episodes, and is never called 'typical'. 'modelled' scoring means no credible source-reported timing exists; a partial restart is recorded but never treated as full reconstitution.

coverage_detail.note: Counts of enumerated events only. A low count may mean genuinely low disruption OR thin open-source reporting for that bucket; this dataset cannot always distinguish the two, and does not pretend to.

estimate_days.basis: Industry source cited by Reuters: repairs to the damaged CDU-10 (~38% of plant capacity) would take at least half a year

recovery.what_source_establishes: Reuters industry source estimated Omsk's damaged CDU-10 would take at least half a year to repair. A credible sourced estimate (medium confidence): its central value drives the modelled horizon for this incident. No restart reported as of the as-of date.

estimate_days.basis: Aggregated industry sources via the Wikipedia strike table expected the refinery offline at least 6 months after the June 2026 strikes

recovery.what_source_establishes: Aggregated, indirect sourcing expected the Moscow Refinery offline at least 6 months after the June 2026 strikes. LOW confidence: the estimate is displayed but is NOT used to drive the decay curve, which falls back to the modelled sector horizon.

recovery.what_source_establishes: Reuters industry sources: Rosneft's Kuibyshev refinery (struck 9-10 June 2026, one episode) resumed operations on 21 August 2026 after major repairs that began 1 July -- ~72 days after the disruption. Establishes a restart to operation, not proven full-capacity reconstitution. A further 28 Aug 2026 strike is after this dataset's as-of date.

UA-CR.name: Crimea
UA-CR.status_note: Separately identified: internationally recognised as Ukraine, under Russian occupation. Not a Russian federal subject. Included in the Monitored-Area ESDI (iteration 4) through the sectors where it has qualifying events and a compatible denominator; excluded from refining/generation for lack of a base. The map does not adjudicate sovereignty through colour or polygon membership.

not_modelled.industrial_impact: No open regional industrial-consumption data ingested.
not_modelled.civilian_electricity_reliability: No outage-duration or customer-minutes-lost data source.
not_modelled.military_industrial: Out of scope: would require mapping defence production to energy supply.
not_modelled.cross_region_dependencies: Requires grid topology and inter-regional flow data not yet ingested.

refinery_reconciliation.national_estimate_source: IEA / Reuters, Russian primary refining ~6.6 mb/d (~330 MTPA)
refinery_reconciliation.note: Tracked major-refinery capacity vs the published national estimate. The gap is chiefly mini-refineries and gas-condensate plants not individually inventoried; refining exposure is measured against tracked capacity and is a lower bound. Unlike facilities are not counted merely to close the gap.

economic_context.provider: Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA)
economic_context.caveat: Observed external economic indicators, monthly. NOT attributed to infrastructure strikes -- export revenue moves for many reasons this data cannot separate. CREA revises historical figures as shipment data is verified; reporting month and snapshot date are preserved.

total_fossil_export_revenue.note: CREA monthly analysis. Observed economic context, not attributed to infrastructure strikes.
CREA: highest revenues in two and a half years.

crude_oil_export_revenue.note: CREA: crude oil export revenue fell 8% m/m in June 2026.

coverage.note: Reported strikes on Russian oil facilities, as tabulated by the source article. Used only to state this dataset's coverage; not an input to any score.
